subject: English Language
curriculum: Zimbabwe Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (MoPSE)
note: Grounded in the official Junior English Language syllabus preamble, aims, objectives, methodology, topics/skills and scope-and-sequence. The syllabus scope-and-sequence and competency-matrix tables were retrieved as scanned/columnar PDF text and portions were not cleanly extractable; grade-by-grade sub-topic content below reflects only what could be reliably read. This should be checked against the source PDF (revision.co.zw/English-Junior.pdf) or a cleaner scan before being treated as exhaustive.

chunks.content: The English Language Junior syllabus covers Grade 3 to Grade 7 as a single document and is built around four basic skills and their sub-skills: Listening/Observing, Speaking/Signing, Reading/Signing, and Writing/Brailling. The naming reflects an inclusive approach: 'Observing' and 'Signing' are included alongside listening and speaking to accommodate learners who are Deaf or hard of hearing, and 'Brailling' is included alongside writing to accommodate learners who are blind or visually impaired. Teaching and learning of visual, manual and tactile skills is emphasised throughout to accommodate learners with diverse learning needs.

The syllabus aims to help learners develop the four basic skills with emphasis on visual, manual and tactile access; express themselves freely in functional English; appreciate English as a tool for cultural, political, religious, social and environmental development; prepare for further studies; promote a reading and creative writing culture; promote the use of ICTs in language learning; and develop basic skills of analysing literary works and communicative competence. As a medium of instruction, English supports learning across the whole curriculum and connects learners to a global language for wider communication.

The syllabus recommends the Functional, Communicative and Multi-Sensory Approaches, operating within a spiral framework so that language forms and structures are taught in context rather than as isolated forms. Recommended methods include Communicative Language Teaching, demonstration, debate and discussion, individual and group presentations, drama, role play/imitation/simulation/miming, poem recitation, educational tours, e-learning, case study, and use of Individual Learning Programmes for learners with special needs. Time allocation for Grade 3 to 7 is 9 periods of 30 minutes per week.

Grade 3 listening work focuses on distinguishing words with long and short vowel sounds, and continues the consolidation and development of phonic skills learnt in previous (Infant) grades. Learners identify silent consonants and vowels in words, and are exposed to Zimbabwean cultural content such as songs, stories about Zimbabwean history, and the Third Chimurenga alongside general listening comprehension of short stories and folktales.
learning_activities: Distinguishing long and short vowel sounds in given word sets
Listening to and retelling short stories and folktales
Listening to stories about Zimbabwean history and heroes/heroines

chunks.content: Grade 4 listening builds on earlier phonic work and introduces homophones (words that sound the same but are spelt differently and carry different meanings, such as 'night/knight' and 'cot/caught'). Learners also practise listening to and following a series of instructions/commands, and listen to material connected to the National Anthem and stories from Zimbabwean history including the Third Chimurenga.
learning_activities: Identifying and discussing homophones from listening passages
Following a series of spoken instructions accurately
Listening to the National Anthem and discussing its message

chunks.topic: Story Telling, Debate and Public Speaking Foundations (Grade 5)
chunks.content: Grade 5 listening and observing work introduces awareness of topical issues, discussion of these issues, and dramatization of topical issues, alongside continued consolidation of phonic skills. Learners are exposed to public speaking foundations such as expressing themselves confidently before an audience and presenting prepared and unprepared speeches, with attention to public speaking skills like self-expression, clarity, posture, gestures and confidence.
learning_activities: Discussing topical issues using appropriate tenses
Presenting prepared and unprepared short speeches
Practising public speaking skills such as posture, gesture and clarity

chunks.content: By Grade 6, listening work emphasises fluency and the use of correct English to narrate topical issues heard over electronic media, including educational programmes. Learners practise using appropriate responses to statements, including short responses requiring true/false or yes/no answers, and continue developing register awareness for different communicative situations.
learning_activities: Listening to and articulating information heard on electronic media programmes
Responding appropriately to statements requiring true/false or yes/no answers
Commenting on programmes heard via electronic media

chunks.topic: Parts of Speech in Spoken Context (Grade 3)
chunks.content: Grade 3 speaking work has learners identifying parts of speech (nouns, pronouns, verbs, prepositions and adjectives) in given texts and constructing meaningful sentences using them in spoken context, alongside practising appropriate forms of greeting, thanking, apologising, requesting and instructing suited to the Zimbabwean context.
learning_activities: Identifying nouns, pronouns, verbs, prepositions and adjectives in spoken sentences
Practising greetings, thanks, apologies, requests and instructions appropriate to context
Comparing Zimbabwean/African and English ways of greeting and requesting

chunks.content: Learners develop and use appropriate register for social interactions such as greetings, introductions, apologies, requests and congratulations, and progress to debating and discussing cross-cutting themes such as the environment, weather and seasons, and natural phenomena like the Hot Springs and sacred places, expressing opinions on these topics using correct English.
learning_activities: Demonstrating appropriate registers in given social situations
Role playing social interactions
Expressing opinions on identified cross-cutting themes such as the environment

chunks.content: Grade 6 speaking work has learners expressing themselves in correct grammar when giving instructions and directions, using compass points and directional phrases (e.g. 'turn left', 'go straight', 'turn south', 'south of', 'to the north of', 'on the left-hand side'), giving and following a series of directions using compasses and maps.
learning_activities: Giving and following directions using the four (and intermediate) compass points
Practising directional phrases with compasses and maps
Role-playing giving instructions and directions to a partner

chunks.content: Learners express views on issues freely and sustain a discussion or argument on topical issues such as child marriages, child labour, child abuse and land reform and other current debatable issues, using argument-sustenance markers such as 'therefore', 'thus', 'subsequently', 'nevertheless' and 'accordingly', developed through debating procedures and presentations on various issues.
learning_activities: Outlining debate procedures
Debating on topical and other current issues
Making presentations on various issues using argument-sustaining language

chunks.content: Grade 3 reading work introduces silent reading for comprehension, reading a range of suitable texts with numbers and pictures for understanding and answering questions, and observing punctuation marks (capital letters, full stops, question marks, commas and paragraphs) while reading.
learning_activities: Reading a variety of texts for comprehension
Answering comprehension questions based on texts
Observing and discussing punctuation marks encountered while reading

chunks.content: Reference skills are introduced from Grade 4 and progressively deepened: learners use the dictionary, atlas, directory and internet for information, extending in later grades to using the index, glossary, table of contents and encyclopaedia sections of reference materials to find and apply information across different learning areas and situations.
learning_activities: Finding information from a dictionary, atlas, directory or internet source
Using the index, glossary and table of contents of a reference book
Applying reference skills to complete a research task in another learning area

chunks.topic: Reading Aloud with Expression and Fluency (Grade 5-6)
chunks.content: Learners progress from proficient silent reading to reading aloud fluently and with expression, observing punctuation marks such as full stops, commas, question marks and exclamation marks, and hand shape/movement (for signing readers), reading with correct stress and intonation, and expressing feelings when reading through use of intonation and non-verbal features.
learning_activities: Reading aloud with correct stress and intonation
Reading passages without regressing, observing punctuation while reading
Reading competitions and expressive reading practice

chunks.topic: Story Elements - Theme, Plot, Characters, Setting (Grade 6)
chunks.content: By Grade 6, reading comprehension extends to analysing the elements of a story: theme (main idea), plot (sequence of events), characters, and setting (time and place). Learners identify the setting, main theme, plot and main/minor characters from texts, and outline the sequence of events, building specific vocabulary and constructing sentences using structures such as conjunctions drawn from the texts read.
learning_activities: Identifying the setting, theme, plot and characters from a text
Outlining the sequence of events in the text
Constructing sentences using vocabulary and structures selected from a text

chunks.content: Handwriting is developed progressively across the Junior grades using the Grade 4-5 Nelson Script/relevant Braille contractions as the reference standard, moving from writing letters with loops and joining them in continuous writing in earlier grades, to legible, well-formed connected writing and correct letter formation with hand-eye coordination (tactile right-to-left for Braille writers) in later grades.
learning_activities: Practising loop letters and joining them in continuous writing
Writing legibly using the Grade 4-5 Nelson Script or relevant Braille contractions
Practising hand-eye coordination and correct pen/stylus grip for handwriting or Braille

chunks.content: Grade 4 writing work has learners identify the basic sentence pattern (Subject + Verb + Object) and construct meaningful sentences from scrambled words using this pattern, laying groundwork for later, more complex sentence and paragraph construction.
learning_activities: Identifying the subject-verb-object pattern in given sentences
Constructing simple sentences using the learnt structure
Re-arranging scrambled sentences into the correct order

chunks.topic: Letter Writing - Formal and Informal (Grade 5-7, progressive)
chunks.content: Letter writing is introduced with informal/friendly letters and extended to formal/business letters as learners progress through the Junior grades, covering letter layout (address, date, salutation, body, closure and signature line for informal letters; two addresses, date, salutation, reference, body, ending 'yours faithfully/sincerely', block paragraphing for formal letters), plus email address conventions. Reasons for writing letters in upper grades include thank-you requests, invitations, applications, complaints, and letters on own affairs and topical issues.
learning_activities: Writing informal/friendly letters using the correct layout
Writing formal/business letters distinguishing their format from informal letters
Creating and using correct email address conventions

chunks.content: Learners progress from writing descriptive paragraphs (identifying features of a paragraph: the topic sentence, developers and terminator) in Grade 6 to full composition writing in Grade 7, covering the structure of a composition (introduction, body/developmental paragraphs, conclusion), use of cohesive markers such as 'at first' and 'later', and writing narrative, descriptive and picture-based compositions, as well as poems, diaries, wall newspapers and reports.
learning_activities: Identifying the topic sentence, developers and terminator of a paragraph
Outlining a composition framework (introduction, body, conclusion)
Writing controlled, guided and free narrative and descriptive compositions
Composing poems and diary/report entries and reading or reciting them to others

chunks.content: Grade 7 grammar-focused writing work covers converting sentences from direct to indirect speech and vice versa (with the accompanying changes in tense, pronouns and punctuation), and the correct use of modal verbs such as 'may', 'might', 'can', 'could', 'will', 'shall', 'should' and 'ought to' in writing sentences.
learning_activities: Writing sentences using modals correctly
Converting sentences from direct to indirect speech and vice versa
Identifying and practising changes in tense and pronouns when converting speech forms

chunks.content: Learners develop note-making skills for their own use across learning areas, and summary writing skills such as providing an appropriate title for a given text, identifying the main ideas of a passage, and maintaining grammatical accuracy and correct punctuation, applied to reorganising, analysing and evaluating information read from a range of texts.
learning_activities: Writing notes and summaries of texts read
Identifying key/main points from a range of texts
Writing a summary in continuous form using appropriate cohesive markers

chunks.content: Learners complete a range of practical written forms accurately, including deposit and withdrawal slips, competitions, bio-data forms, indemnity forms, application forms and medical aid forms, connecting writing skills to real-life, everyday and enterprise-related documentation.
learning_activities: Reading instructions on a variety of practical forms
Completing different types of forms correctly
Discussing the purpose of common forms encountered in daily life

chunks.content: The English Language syllabus integrates cross-cutting themes across all four skills: Gender, Children's Rights and Responsibilities, Child Protection, Disaster Risk Management, Financial Literacy, Sexuality/HIV and AIDS Education, Heritage Studies, Collaboration, and Environmental Issues. These themes are woven into listening, speaking, reading and writing activities (e.g. discussing child marriage or child labour in debate work, or environmental issues in reading and speaking tasks) rather than taught as separate content.
